model_output.verdict: An outpatient physical therapist with a clear caseload, a rehab program, and patient-reported results.
write_up: Your resume makes a strong case for outpatient orthopedic work! At North Loop, you show the patients you treat, the program you built, and how discharged patients reported their function. A recruiter can move forward knowing what your clinical work looks like.

The return-to-run program is a model for the rest: it names what you built and how many patients completed it. Your license and DPT are easy to find, and your hospital role adds orthopedic, neurological, and fall-prevention work.

The main detail to add is the measure behind the discharged-patient result. Your resume is unlikely to be the reason someone passes on its own; the match with a clinic's patient population and how competitive the opening is will matter too.

cards.line: - Built a return-to-run program that 85 patients completed in 2025
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It gives the program a name and puts a count beside the patients who completed it, without claiming more than that.

cards.line: - In 2025, 92% of discharged patients improved their patient-reported function scores
cards.cannot_tell: This is a useful patient result, but a recruiter can't tell which function measure you used or how many discharged patients are behind the percentage. Those details give the result context.
cards.example: In 2025, 92% of [number] discharged patients improved their patient-reported function scores on [measure]
cards.question: Which function measure did you use, and how many discharged patients were included in the percentage?
